authorisation: The same Product-Owner closure mission recorded at T0175, which authorised controlled PRE-LIVE work by name: deployment, service restarts, migrations, VLAN networking, DHCP, database backup/restore and rollback drills, security hardening and failure drills on 172.21.60.25. UNLIKE increments 2 and 3, this one took those actions. No new authorisation was sought or needed, and nothing outside that list was done: no Go-Live, no guest activation, no real PMS financial posting, no payment-provider traffic, and 172.21.60.23 was not contacted.

what_this_increment_is.headline: The PRE-LIVE operational drills the closure was waiting on. Every one of them found something, which is the point of running a drill rather than reasoning about it.
what_this_increment_is.service_user_separation: CLOSED. portald listened on *:8380 -- every guest VLAN -- as User=stayconnect, the same account as edged, and /run/stayconnect/scd.sock is root:stayconnect 0660. So the network-facing process could call /v1/backup/restore, /v1/license/install, /v1/setup/enroll and the voucher code reveal directly, with no operator, no permission check and no step-up, because all of those live in edged and nothing proved they had happened. The voucher reveal is what made it urgent in increment 3 and was never the worst of it. The recorded fix -- 'the socket group admits edged only' -- turned out to be WRONG: the captive portal authenticates guests through that socket, so removing its access removes guest internet. What was narrowed instead is the surface. portald has its own uid (a uid check means nothing under a shared uid, because one process can ptrace the other), and cmd/scd/admin_surface.go classifies all 56 routes and requires an administrative one to come from edged BY UID. Classification defaults to admin, so a route added and forgotten is refused rather than exposed, and a test walks the registered routes and fails when any is unclassified. Proven live: uid 995 got 403 on five admin routes and 200 on the guest ones, uid 998 got 200 on all five, root was admitted deliberately, scd logged every refusal with peer_uid=995 expected_uid=998, and portald itself then called /v1/tenant/branding and /v1/tenant/auth-methods through the socket and got real data back.
what_this_increment_is.backup_restore_drill: CLOSED, and it found four defects. (1) The restore could not run at all: it called host pg_restore as role `stayconnect_site`, and this appliance has no host pg_restore and no such role -- both things the BACKUP half had already been corrected for. The --dry-run passes on a machine where the real run cannot work, and the marker is advanced and five writers stopped in the steps after it, so the failure mode was an appliance with its services down and its database untouched. (2) `pg_restore --clean --if-exists` DESTROYS this database: it drops the TimescaleDB extension with everything else, takes _timescaledb_functions and _timescaledb_internal with it, and 72 dependent objects then fail. Measured: 96 relational tables intact, no extension, both hypertables empty. (3) The management marker was written 0600 root-owned, and edged -- its only reader -- runs unprivileged, so a REAL supported restore produced outcome=UNCHANGED with no hold and no record, because ReadRestoreMarker treated EACCES as absence on the reasoning that absence only ever causes more holding. That is false at generation zero, which is where every appliance starts. (4) No operator could release the recovery: p4_assert_financial_actor requires operators.tenant_id, which the appliance leaves NULL by documented convention, so all four actor-gated financial kernels were unperformable here. All four fixed, then the whole path re-run end to end: manifest verified against the pinned anchor, generation 1 to 2, five writers proven stopped, database recreated, timescaledb suspended and restored, Gate-P re-applied, 2 hypertables registered, epoch 2 RESTORE_DETECTED recorded as SUPPORTED with the signed manifest's digest, money movement held, then released through the same kernel the operator screen calls.
what_this_increment_is.tagged_multi_vlan_acceptance: CLOSED. phase19-network-test.sh was run on PRE-LIVE for the first time since T0175 made it appliance-independent: ALL GREEN, 11 checks. A new drill then proved the plural the gap actually named, ALL GREEN, 21 checks: two tagged VLANs coexisting off ONE trunk with neither apply removing the other, a gateway per bridge, Kea carrying both subnets at once with each advertising its OWN option-114 URL, a real DORA on each from its own pool, nftables holding state for both networks, and the management address untouched.

With Central blackholed: the licence still evaluates Active from the local store, scd logging 'initial cloud license fetch failed (offline-safe)'; the whole operator surface answers 200; a guest device leases from the live guest network; and a voucher is VALIDATED by iam_v2 against the appliance's own data, with the auth_contexts and devices rows to show it. defects_this_increment_found_in_its_own_.the_deployed_scd_was_not_a_production_bu: The most serious finding, and mine. I built and deployed scd from a recipe I had recorded as 'no build tags == the production profile'. That is false. enforceGuestAuthorityLock forces the VOUCHER and ACCOUNT guest methods on, and it is keyed on the `stayconnect_production` BUILD TAG, deliberately not on the productionProfile argument, 'because which IAM authority is in force is decided by the binary, not by an argument or an env file'. Untagged, the lock never ran, and a guest presenting a valid voucher got IAMV2_UNAVAILABLE (503) while the Hotel Admin Sign-in methods screen reported vouchers enabled. Only the binary I had touched was affected; the other five were production builds. Rebuilt with scripts/build-appliance-binaries.sh, which exists for exactly this reason and also forbids the strip my hand-rolled build did. After redeploying: 'iamv2 master=true VOUCHER=true ACCOUNT=true ... build=production'.
defects_this_increment_found_in_its_own_.migration_0090_failed_the_disaster_recov: 0090 asserted that every iam_v2 table is owned by iam_v2_owner. On the factory-clean path the migrations run as the cluster superuser, so their tables are owned by `stayconnect` and ownership moves to iam_v2_owner afterwards in Gate-P -- which runs AFTER the migrations on both install paths, making the file's own 'migrations assert, Gate-P establishes' impossible in that order. The assertion failed the whole reconstruction. Narrowed to the invariant a migration can honestly carry at its own point in the sequence: no iam_v2 table is owned by iam_v2_migrator, which is order-independent and catches exactly the defect 0089 corrected. The full invariant is still asserted at the end of gatep-grants.sql, where it is true. Edited in place, because an 0091 would not stop 0090 failing on every future clean install.
defects_this_increment_found_in_its_own_.docker_cp_applied_a_stale_file: `docker cp <dir> <container>:<path>` copies INTO path when path exists. A second Gate-P run put the files at /tmp/gatep/gatep/... and applied the FIRST run's copy, reporting success while the new grant was simply absent. Both scripts now remove the target first.
defects_this_increment_found_in_its_own_.three_false_results_in_my_own_drills: A refusal-only isolation test that a refuse-everything gate would pass, so every refusal is now paired with the admission it must not break. A JSON POST to a FORM handler that returned the portal page with HTTP 200, where a loose grep for 'success' matched that HTML and reported a pass no session existed for. And a session count keyed by client IP, where the DHCP pool had recycled the address and a stale row made before/after counts meaningless.
defects_this_increment_found_in_its_own_.a_drill_that_blamed_the_product_for_its_: The multi-VLAN drill's first run reported ten failures, all caused by its own cleanup confirming a revision without revision_id: netd decoded an empty uuid, the ncr_single_inflight index then refused the drill's own apply, and the apply body was swallowed and printed as 'state=None'. Its third run rolled back with 'kea is still not listening on ... after a restart', and THAT was netd being right -- Kea will not bind a gateway on a bridge with no carrier, and the health check rolled the apply back rather than leave a guest network handing out no addresses, with the management address untouched. Earlier runs had passed on timing rather than on carrier, which is worse than failing.
defects_this_increment_found_in_its_own_.the_gate_found_one_more_of_mine: phase4-financial-core-gate refused PR #177 on two restore-drill cases: 'a writer that will not stop aborts the restore' and 'the marker is advanced before the quiesce'. A real consequence of a deliberate change, not a flake. The restore now resolves its database access BEFORE advancing the marker and before stopping any writer, because of the PRE-LIVE failure where it discovered a missing client and a non-existent role only AFTER the marker was advanced and five writers stopped. A fixture with no database therefore aborts at that check and never reaches the quiesce those two cases are about. THE FIXTURE WAS FIXED, NOT THE CHECK -- the drill already runs a disposable PostgreSQL, so that case now points the tool at it. Relaxing the reachability check to keep an old fixture working would have discarded the protection it exists for, and the gate would then have been green about a restore path that cannot run. RESTORE DRILL: PASS=39 FAIL=0.
defects_this_increment_found_in_its_own_.the_review_found_a_hole_in_my_own_fix:
THE MOST SERIOUS FINDING OF THE INCREMENT, and it was in the fix for the previous most serious one. An automated review of PR #177 raised three findings and the ruleset correctly blocked the merge on them. All three were real.

(1) After portald got its own account, peer_identity_linux.go claimed the uid was 'now the load-bearing one'. It was not: stayconnect-hotel-admin.service ran /usr/bin/node server.js as User=stayconnect, and the next-server process reported Uid 998 Gid 998 -- exactly edged's -- with a group that opens scd.sock. So the Node process rendering the ADMIN WEB UI was admitted to /v1/backup/restore, /v1/license/install and /v1/setup/enroll with none of edged's operator authentication, permission check or step-up. Six Go services had been enumerated and the one written in another language was not. Fixed in both halves: the administrative surface now requires the peer's EXECUTABLE as well as its uid (sharing one comparison with the code-recovery gate), and hotel-admin has its own account with NO supplementary group, because it never opens the socket at all. Verified live: uid 998 with a different image gets 403 and scd logs 'sharing edged's uid but running a different image'; hotel-admin at uid 994 cannot open the socket at all; edged still works; the guest portal still serves; the admin UI passes 23 browser checks. Every service now has its own identity and edged is the only holder of the stayconnect account.

(2) An EMPTY ledger was read as a hundred gaps. The baseline is 'the CURRENT schema and only the current schema' and inserts no schema_migrations rows, so a freshly provisioned appliance has an empty ledger, the derived floor is empty, and every historical file counts as missing -- the first apply on every newly provisioned appliance would have been refused. The check now skips on an empty ledger and says why. The better fix is in the baseline generator and is recorded rather than done in passing.

(3) The gap check ran BEFORE the ledger lock, so a concurrent rollback could remove a predecessor between the check and the write. The exact set is now re-asserted inside the lock, and the refusal is named rather than falling through to a generic runner error.

EDGE_MIGRATE_SELFTEST = PASS (37 cases). The race case was made DETERMINISTIC after its first version slept and reported that the ordering had not occurred -- an honest non-result that left the guard unexercised.

install_path_defects_found_while_there.accounts_no_install_path_created: stayconnect-pmsd.service has named User=stayconnect-pmsd since Phase 3 and nothing ever created that account. It works on this appliance because somebody ran useradd by hand; a factory-clean provision would have installed the unit and left pmsd dead with 'Failed to determine user credentials'. Both install paths now create the accounts the units name, DERIVED from the units rather than from a hand-written list -- the list that already fell behind once and filled the root filesystem.
install_path_defects_found_while_there.libraries_no_install_path_created: lib-hotel-admin-contract.sh sits in /opt/stayconnect/bin with no line in the repository putting it there. A helper installed into $BIN loses its directory, so anything it sources from 'next to me' must be next to it THERE. The installer now carries lib-*.sh too.
install_path_defects_found_while_there.tmpfiles_only_a_fresh_install_ever_appli: deploy/tmpfiles declares paths that sandboxed units need to EXIST BEFORE THEY START, because systemd resolves ReadWritePaths at unit start. Only provision-fresh-appliance.sh copied them, so a change to any of those declarations reached a fresh install and nothing else.

evidence: Every claim above was produced by running something on 172.21.60.25 or on a disposable cluster, and the output is in the commit messages of the ten content commits between the base and the head of this increment. The two new harnesses are in the repository rather than in a transcript: scripts/phase19-multi-vlan-test.sh and scripts/central-outage-local-first-test.sh, plus hotel-admin/test/verify-vouchers-ui.mjs for the browser check.
what_this_increment_did_not_do: It did not enable any guest capability. Guest voucher AUTHENTICATION works and is proven live; a SESSION additionally requires an entitlement from the commerce grant, and Phase 2 is dark, so the voucher correctly stays UNUSED and no guest received internet access. THAT BOUNDARY WAS ALREADY RECORDED AND ALREADY DECIDED -- open_product_owner_decisions.guest_sign_in_methods_on_pre_live describes it exactly and was RESOLVED as deferred under D41 on 2026-09-22 -- so this increment re-measured it rather than discovered it, and that entry now carries the fresh evidence. Device Self-Service was not exercised end to end: its enabling harness refuses to run anywhere but a compiled-in allow-list naming the RETIRED development appliance, and that refusal is deliberately not overridable, so closing it needs a decision. Nothing was done about HA, no payment provider was selected, and no external receipt authority was created.
go_live: NOT authorised and not performed. D41 remains in force: real Guest activation and Guest pilot use stay deferred. PRE-LIVE remains PRE-LIVE.
